title: Select the durable released attempt for an expansion parent
description: Second prerequisite for atomic graph.request_expansion persistence. Provide a production read-only selector that starts from the authenticated project plus the durable goal/parent planning-run and active-graph parent node, discovers the unique Foundation attempt released for that parent, and then composes task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4's strict readCurrentExpansionRelease({attemptRef, projectId}). No caller may supply attemptRef and no release authority may be reconstructed from advisory rows.
definitionOfDone: Verify the complete production provenance before implementation: measure the approved-run/GoalExecutionEnabled witness, parent PlanningRun record, active graph membership, Foundation activation/attempt records, release locator/record, and readCurrentExpansionRelease reader. Name the earliest durable producer and exact join keys for project + goal + parentRunRef + parentNodeRef -> attemptRef; if no unambiguous current-byte join exists within focused scope, report blocked and carve the producer leaf rather than guessing recency or adding fixture authority.

Define an exact immutable query/result/refusal contract for the server-owned selector. The query accepts no caller release evidence or attemptRef; every refusal has a closed exact code plus layer, missing/malformed/foreign/ambiguous/raced evidence returns ok:false, and success is advisory only until the existing e62 reader verifies the candidate.

TDD builds a production-reachable reader that verifies the parent run belongs to the named goal/project, the parent node belongs to the one active graph for that goal/world, discovers candidate attempt identity only from durable producer records, and composes readCurrentExpansionRelease without reimplementing its safe-boundary, terminal-effect, resource, decision-trace, handoff, or release-consistency checks.

The selector returns success only for exactly one fully verified RELEASED attempt bound to the same project/goal/parent run/node. Zero candidates, duplicate/retry candidates without a durable current winner, foreign or cross-spliced run/node/attempt facts, malformed bytes, store faults, pagination truncation/horizon growth, and concurrent mutation all refuse with their exact code/layer and grant no authority.

A named immutable nonzero hostile-case roster covers every selector refusal and server-owned field; tests assert the exact roster count, exact code plus layer, positive reachable success denominator, deep immutability/copying, close/reopen replay, and a deletion drill proving removal of the production join or e62 call makes the intended tests red.

Export the selector only through the established daemon production root needed by the parent consumer, keep source files focused at repository size targets, and pass fresh foreground pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm verify:foundation, and pnpm verify:store gates with explicit exit codes.
taskRails: Read-only daemon leaf: do not create the expansion hold or PlanningRun and do not edit the store decision transaction in this task.
attemptRef is always server-derived from durable production facts; caller payload/envelope types must not gain attemptRef, release, decisionTrace, or any authority-bearing surrogate.
Compose readCurrentExpansionRelease from task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4 verbatim; do not fork, weaken, seed, or reconstruct its proof.
Never select by timestamp, row order, maximum id, first/last match, or an advisory FoundationAttemptRecorded row alone. Ambiguity and unverifiable linkage fail closed.
Keep goal, approved parent run, active graph revision/node, Foundation attempt, and released safe-boundary truth distinct and cross-check every project/identity edge.

If a missing durable parent-run/attempt correlation requires a new writer or contract field outside a focused reader slice, stop and create a separately ordered producer task rather than widening this selector invisibly.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the exact immutable server-only contract in a focused module and its one-line .js bridge. Admit only the four exact keys `[goalRef,parentNodeRef,parentRunRef,projectId]` as bounded nonempty text; any extra key, including attemptRef/release/decisionTrace, refuses. Publish frozen code and layer rosters. Use the closed local codes REQUEST_INVALID, STORE_UNAVAILABLE, STORE_PROJECT_MISMATCH, PARENT_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE, APPROVED_RUN_UNAVAILABLE, PARENT_RUN_MISMATCH, GRAPH_BINDING_MISMATCH, LOCATOR_SCAN_INCOMPLETE, LOCATOR_EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE, LOCATOR_BINDING_MISMATCH, ATTEMPT_ABSENT, ATTEMPT_AMBIGUOUS, ACTIVATION_UNAVAILABLE, ACTIVATION_MISMATCH, RELEASE_UNAVAILABLE and CURRENTNESS_MOVED (all with the `EXPANSION_RELEASE_SELECTOR_` prefix). Define an exact refusal `{ok:false,code,layer,sourceCode,sourceLayer}` and final success `{ok:true,attemptRef,release,workerHandoff}`; factories must copy and deep-freeze nested values. Candidate discovery remains internal and gains no advisory success result.

Admission — `admitExpansionReleaseSelectorQuery`: rejects non-objects and arrays; requires `Reflect.ownKeys(query).length === 4`; requires every own key to be a STRING member of `EXPANSION_RELEASE_SELECTOR_QUERY_KEYS`; requires each to be an own ENUMERABLE DATA property (`"value" in descriptor`), so an accessor is refused rather than invoked and four unrelated keys cannot fall through to a prototype getter; then requires all four to be bounded non-empty text (`MAX_TEXT` 256, matching e62's own ceiling so a ref this selector admits cannot be one e62 would refuse). implementationPlan.description: Implement the bounded locator scan in a second focused module and bridge. Capture an externally supplied horizon, page only `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_EVENT_TYPE` with `readEventsByTypeAfter`, validate page shape/type/global-position monotonicity and completion through that horizon, inspect every row, and never early-return. Decode the paged event, derive its slot identity, strict-read the aggregate with `readFoundationContextManifest` so canonical payload, aggregate identity, decision and receipt are all proven, and byte-compare the paged row to the strict read. Parse the digest-verified `manifest.binding.exactBytes` as the canonical newline-delimited context items and require exactly one correctly shaped mandatory foundation.graph, foundation.approved-plan, foundation.objective and foundation.activation item. Cross-check projectId, goalRef, parentRunRef, parentNodeRef, active graph revision/hash/epoch/planHash, approved authority/revision/run, attemptRef and sessionId. Valid unrelated nodes/revisions may be ignored only after strict verification; malformed, foreign/cross-spliced or duplicate mandatory facts refuse. Return all exact matching locator candidates so the orchestrator, not row order, decides zero/one/many.

Implement the production selector and bridge in dependency order. First broaden `ExpansionRequestAuthorityInput.payload` to a Pick of goalRef/parentNodeRef/parentRunRef (the existing full request remains structurally compatible), then reuse `readDurableLedger` plus `readExpansionRequestAuthority` to verify the durable goal, PlanningRun, active graph and node without fabricating rationale. Capture the global horizon; verify store project health; call `readApprovedPlan` and require its GoalExecutionEnabled-backed runId, graphRevisionRef and planHash to equal the query/current graph; run the full locator scan; refuse zero or more-than-one candidate; call `readFoundationActivationByAttempt` and require attempt/project/session equality; then call `readCurrentExpansionRelease(store,{attemptRef,projectId})` verbatim. Wrap upstream failures in the closed selector refusal while retaining sourceCode/sourceLayer. Re-read the global horizon last and refuse movement. Only after e62 returns BOUND, return a copied/deep-frozen final success. Export both the direct reader and a store-bound `ExpansionReleaseAuthorityReader` factory for the parent consumer; add no writer, hold, PlanningRun or transaction change.
implementationPlan.note:
`expansion-release-selector.ts` (251 lines) + `.js` bridge. Order, exactly as planned:

1. `admitExpansionReleaseSelectorQuery` (REQUEST_INVALID before any store touch).
2. `store.getHealth().projectId` — mismatch -> STORE_PROJECT_MISMATCH, throw -> STORE_UNAVAILABLE.
3. `store.readEventHorizon()` captured ONCE; a throw is STORE_UNAVAILABLE and a non-bigint/negative value is LOCATOR_SCAN_INCOMPLETE.
4. `readExpansionRequestAuthority({ledger: readDurableLedger(...), payload: {goalRef, parentNodeRef, parentRunRef}, projectId, store})` — durable goal, PlanningRun ownership, active graph and node membership. NO rationale is fabricated: the input type was narrowed (below) so a placeholder is unrepresentable rather than merely unread. Refusal -> PARENT_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE carrying the authority's own code and `sourceLayer ?? layer`.
5. `currentGraph` — this module's OWN second `readCurrentActiveGraph`, required to agree with the authority on revisionId/graphContentHash/graphEpoch/goalRef. Two reads are the point: the authority proves the parent sits in a current graph, this proves the SAME graph is still current when the plan's binding is judged. Refusal -> GRAPH_BINDING_MISMATCH.
6. `approvedPlan` — GoalExecutionEnabled-backed `readApprovedPlan`; refusal -> APPROVED_RUN_UNAVAILABLE with the reader's code/layer; `plan.runId !== parentRunRef` -> PARENT_RUN_MISMATCH; `plan.graphRevisionRef !== graph.revisionId` -> GRAPH_BINDING_MISMATCH.
7. `scanExpansionReleaseCandidates(store, expectation, horizon)`; zero -> ATTEMPT_ABSENT, more than one -> ATTEMPT_AMBIGUOUS. No ordering tie-break exists.
8. `readFoundationActivationByAttempt`; not BOUND -> ACTIVATION_UNAVAILABLE with its code/layer; attempt/project/session disagreement -> ACTIVATION_MISMATCH.
9. `readCurrentExpansionRelease(store, {attemptRef: candidate.attemptRef, projectId})` VERBATIM. Not BOUND -> RELEASE_UNAVAILABLE carrying e62's code and layer — measured as `ATTEMPT_RELEASE_RECORD_ABSENT` / `DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RELEASE`, i.e. e62 forwarding its own source rather than restamping it.
10. Final `readEventHorizon()`; any movement -> CURRENTNESS_MOVED. Only then `deepFreezeSelection({attemptRef, ok:true, release, workerHandoff})`.

Upstream edit, forced and minimal: `ExpansionRequestAuthorityInput.payload` narrowed from `ExpansionRequestPayload` to `Pick<…, "goalRef"|"parentNodeRef"|"parentRunRef">`. The three-line deletion is a compile requirement, not a design change — and it upgrades the placeholder from "unread" to "unrepresentable".

PRODUCTION DEFECT FIXED HERE: `isRefused` was `(value: object) => "ok" in value`. `ActiveGraphAccepted` and `ApprovedPlanRead` BOTH carry `ok: true`, so the presence test answered "refused" for every SUCCESS and `readExpansionReleaseSelection` returned the graph projection wearing this module's success shape — `{ok:true}` with no `attemptRef` and no `release`, and no candidate scan, no activation check and no e62 call ever ran. Measured as 20 failing arms; now `!value.ok`.

Also fixed here (paired with step-4's): `plan.planHash !== graph.planHash` dropped from `approvedPlan`; the plan hash is now checked against the plan ITEM in the sealed manifest instead of against the graph revision's unrelated hash.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: use the committed pre-launch Foundation context-manifest event as the earliest durable attempt locator. Its outer record binds projectId, nodeKey, graph revision/hash/epoch, attemptRef and sessionId; its digest-bound exactBytes also contains the mandatory foundation.graph, foundation.approved-plan, foundation.objective and foundation.activation items. Strictly read those bytes, cross-check them against the current durable goal/PlanningRun, GoalExecutionEnabled-approved run and active graph, then call readCurrentExpansionRelease unchanged.
Rejected: accept attemptRef/release/decisionTrace from the caller; select the newest/first/last advisory attempt; or try every attempt and keep whichever e62 accepts. Each would let ordering or caller material mint authority and would hide retries rather than refusing ambiguity.
Rejected: infer parentRunRef only from a matching current graph revision. A revision may be reused, so the selector must also extract and compare the digest-bound foundation.approved-plan.runId and the graph/goal item from the launched context.
Rejected: add parent-run fields to the release writer/record. The current committed context bytes already carry the direct run correlation, so widening a writer is unnecessary and violates this read-only leaf. If that direct item is absent when work starts, block and carve a producer task rather than weakening the join.
Rejected: copy safe-boundary, terminal, resource, decision-trace, handoff or release checks. The final candidate goes through task-e62's readCurrentExpansionRelease(store,{attemptRef,projectId}) verbatim.

planningNotes.risks:
The attempt-to-run correlation is in the context manifest's digest-bound canonical exactBytes, not a top-level runId field. The parser must require exactly one correctly shaped mandatory item for graph, approved plan, objective and activation; missing, duplicate, noncanonical or cross-spliced items refuse.
Never stop the typed scan after finding a match. A later matching retry must turn the result into ATTEMPT_AMBIGUOUS, and malformed/truncated later pages must still refuse.
A matching context row is only a locator. It must be strict-read with its command decision/receipt and aggregate identity, checked against activation/session, and then passed to e62. No intermediate candidate is returned as success.
Bracket the whole multi-reader composition with one global event horizon. Component-level currentness checks do not prove the composed world stayed fixed.
Keep each new production file at or below the repository target of 250 lines. Do not edit the existing 304-line e62 reader or any foreign-dirty context/attempt files.
Test fixtures must invoke landed production persistence/writers to build the approved goal/run/graph/context/activation/release world. They may corrupt a copied/on-disk test store for hostile arms, but must not seed a test-only authority path.
The deletion drill will target new, initially untracked modules. Follow the SHA256 out-of-tree backup/restore rule rather than relying on git diff.
